pages.text: A fault-tolerant quantum computer. Each logical qubit is a surface-code patch of 2d² physical qubits; the logical error falls as (p/p_th)^((d+1)/2) - if the physical error p is below 1%. And p depends on temperature: hf/kT must be large, or thermal excitations flip the qubits.
$(thing)Set$(): Code distance d, Qubit frequency, Gate clock, Logical qubits.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Control-line crosstalk: gate errors grow by 20%·|d|.
$(thing)Limits$(): Above the threshold: error correction makes things worse.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Logical operations per second.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Thermal error: p_th = e^(−hf/kT)$(br)Gate error: p_g$(br)Physical error p: p = p_g + p_th$(br)Logical error: p_L = 0.1(p/p_th)^((d+1)/2)$(br)Physical qubits: N = 2d²·N_L$(br)Wiring heat: P ∝ N·√f_clk·f_q
